setting.FORCE_LLM_SUMMARY_ON_MERGE: How many descriptions it takes to trigger a summary.
setting.ENABLE_LLM_CACHE_FOR_EXTRACT: Reuses earlier results when a document is reprocessed.
setting.VLM_LLM_MODEL: The model. It must support images.
setting.VLM_PROCESS_ENABLE: Turns vision on or off for documents and emails.
setting.VLM_MIN_IMAGE_PIXEL: Skips tiny images, in documents and emails.
setting.VLM_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES: Largest image sent, in documents and emails.
setting.KEYWORD_LLM_MODEL: The model. A small, fast one is usually enough.
setting.ENABLE_LLM_CACHE: Reuses the result when the same question is asked again.
setting.QUERY_LLM_MODEL: The model. Usually the largest cost decision.
setting.MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS: Upper limit on context for each answer.
setting.TOP_K: How many entities and relationships are retrieved.
setting.CHUNK_TOP_K: How many text chunks are kept.

cancelling.label: Cancelling
cancelling.explain: A user asked to cancel the run. It stops after the documents in progress; it still holds the workspace until then.

paused.label: Paused
paused.explain: The LLM provider rejected requests (for example budget or rate limit), so the run stopped. It resumes when the pause clears.

hung.label: Hung
hung.explain: The worker is alive but no document has made progress for longer than the hung threshold.

orphaned.label: Orphaned
orphaned.explain: The worker that owned this run has exited (confirmed by the operating system). Busy stays set until it is released or the container restarts.

busy_without_run.label: Busy without a run
busy_without_run.explain: The workspace is marked busy but no live run owns it, for example after an upgrade or a crash.

reservation.label: Stranded reservation
reservation.explain: A scan or enqueue reservation has no live owner and blocks email drains. Restart the container to clear it.

stale_doc.label: Stale document
stale_doc.explain: The document has been in progress for longer than the stale-document threshold.

unresponsive.label: Unresponsive
unresponsive.explain: The worker that owns this run stopped sending heartbeats, but its process is not confirmed gone, so the run is not orphaned. It still holds the workspace.

succeeded.label: Succeeded
succeeded.explain: The run finished and processed its documents.

failed.label: Failed
failed.explain: The run stopped on an error. Its documents stay failed or pending and are retried by the next run.

cancelled.label: Cancelled
cancelled.explain: A user cancelled the run. Cancelled documents are retried automatically by the next run.

unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.explain: The state of this run could not be determined.

llm.label: LLM provider
llm.role: Answers extraction, keyword, query and vision calls.
llm.watch: Passive only, so no paid test calls: error rate, latency and provider rejections from the usage table.

smtp.label: SMTP
smtp.role: Sends provider, budget and operations alert emails.
smtp.watch: EHLO, STARTTLS and NOOP every 15 minutes. No mail is sent.

browser.label: Admins and users
browser.role: Everyone reaches the WebUI and the API through the server's HTTP stack.
browser.watch: The Operations tab polls /admin/ops only for the visible view and pauses while the browser tab is hidden.

connector.label: Email connector
connector.role: Posts emails to /documents/email. Re-sent emails are deferred to the queue directory.
connector.watch: Email queue depth, the oldest record and drain attempts per workspace (Processing › Email queue).

clients.label: API clients
clients.watch: Request IDs on every response; HTTP latency and 5xx per route under Performance › HTTP.

proxy.label: Reverse proxy
proxy.role: Terminates TLS and forwards requests to LightRAG. It may also route callers straight to vLLM.
proxy.watch: A TLS certificate expiry check every 15 minutes. Its own logs are out of scope.

http.label: HTTP stack
http.role: Uvicorn, the middleware (request ID, usage context, security headers, CORS) and the routers.
http.watch: Every response carries X-Request-ID, and error messages show it as Ref:.

opsapi.label: /admin/ops API
opsapi.role: The endpoints behind this console, admin-only for the whole router.
opsapi.watch: Short per-process caches keep the cost flat however many admins watch. It never loads a workspace into memory.

pipeline.label: Ingestion pipeline
pipeline.role: Parses documents, extracts entities with the LLM and merges them into the graph and vector stores. One run per workspace at a time.
pipeline.watch: Active runs, stuck documents and failures (Processing).

drainer.label: Email re-sync drainers
drainer.role: Apply deferred email bundles in batches, with backoff while the workspace is busy.
drainer.watch: Per-workspace attempts and last result (Processing › Email queue); live drainers per worker (Workers).

insights.label: Insights recorder
insights.role: Writes one usage row per LLM call for Token Insights and the LLM health numbers here.
insights.watch: Buffer, last flush, lost rows and dropped events from each worker's heartbeat.

collectors.label: Ops collectors
collectors.role: Every process writes its own heartbeat. One leased copy per host runs the probes (30 s) and the attention check.
collectors.watch: Switch to the Monitoring layer to see what they write and what they probe.

queue.label: Queue directory
queue.role: One file per deferred email bundle under the working directory.
queue.watch: Counted without opening files, so email contents never reach the console.

postgres.label: PostgreSQL
postgres.role: KV storage, document status, Insights usage tables and the operations tables.
postgres.watch: SELECT 1 latency on a dedicated connection; connections against the limit and blocked queries every 5 minutes.

graph.label: Graph store
graph.watch: A connectivity check on its own driver every 30 seconds.

vector.label: Vector store
vector.role: Vector storage for chunks, entities and relations.
vector.watch: A health check on its own client every 30 seconds. Synchronous client calls also show up as event-loop lag on the workers.

etcd.label: etcd
etcd.watch: Not probed directly. A Milvus health failure is the signal.

minio.label: MinIO
minio.watch: Not probed directly. A Milvus health failure is the signal.

vembed.label: Embeddings
vembed.watch: /health, plus running, waiting and KV cache from /metrics when it is readable. Waiting includes callers outside LightRAG.

vrerank.label: Reranker
vrerank.watch: /health, plus running, waiting and KV cache from /metrics when it is readable. Waiting includes callers outside LightRAG.

docling.label: Docling
docling.role: Parses PDF, Office and other rich documents.

blocking.title: Blocked and blocking sessions
blocking.none: No blocked sessions at the last check.
blocking.note: Statement type, a query fingerprint and its length only; query text and parameters are never shown.

note.vllm: Waiting counts every caller of this endpoint, including any that reach it directly through the proxy. Compare it with LightRAG's own call rate before blaming LightRAG load.
note.milvus: Milvus depends on etcd and MinIO; check those containers too. Its client calls are synchronous, so while it hangs the workers' event-loop lag rises.
note.vector: Vector store calls can block the event loop while the store is slow; check the workers' loop lag too.
note.llm: Passive check: no paid test call is made. Health comes from real calls in the usage table: error rate, latency and provider rejections.
note.smtp: The probe and the test connect, say EHLO, STARTTLS and NOOP, then quit. No mail is ever sent.
note.postgres: Probed on a dedicated connection, so a busy pool does not hide the database's own latency.

cancel.title: Cancel processing in {{workspace}}
cancel.body: Soft cancel. Documents already queued for parse or analyze still go through those steps. Cancelled documents become FAILED ("User cancelled…") and are retried automatically by the next run, including the email re-sync about every 70 minutes.

run.title: Run pipeline now in {{workspace}}
run.body: Retries every pending and failed document in {{workspace}}, user-cancelled ones included. It is refused while a provider pause is active, unless you tick "override pause".
run.preview: Will process {{pending}} pending + {{failed}} failed (including {{cancelled}} user-cancelled) docs in {{workspace}}.
run.previewInterrupted_one: Plus {{count}} document left mid-pipeline by an interrupted run.
run.previewInterrupted_other: Plus {{count}} documents left mid-pipeline by an interrupted run.
run.previewNothing: Nothing is waiting in {{workspace}}: a run would find no documents.
run.overrideHint: Only after the provider limit was raised. Otherwise the run stops again at the first call.
run.overridePaused: A provider pause is active. Without this the run is refused.
run.previewLoading: Counting what a run would process…
run.previewFailed: The dry run did not answer.

meets.busy: The pipeline is busy right now, so a run would be refused until it ends.
meets.destructive: A deletion or clear is running, so a run would be refused until it ends.
meets.paused: A provider pause is active: tick "override pause" to run anyway.

drain.title: Drain the email queue for {{workspace}}
drain.body_one: Asks the drainer for {{count}} queued record to retry now. If the pipeline is busy it keeps retrying with backoff.
drain.body_other: Asks the drainer for {{count}} queued records to retry now. If the pipeline is busy it keeps retrying with backoff.
drain.bodyUnknown: Asks the drainer to retry this workspace's queued records now. If the pipeline is busy it keeps retrying with backoff.
drain.limits: At most once a minute per workspace. Unreadable (.bad) files are never touched.

release.title: Release busy in {{workspace}}
release.onlyGone: Only for a worker that is gone.
release.noOwner: No owner is recorded for this busy flag, so the server cannot confirm its worker is gone and will refuse the release. Restart the container if the workspace stays stuck.
release.body: Releasing lets new work start; partial docs are retried; queued "process again" requests are kept.
release.frozen: If the worker is alive but frozen, restart the container instead.
release.liveFailed: The live state could not be read, so busy cannot be released safely. Close this and try again.
release.notBusy: The pipeline is no longer busy: there is nothing to release.

reservations.title: Release reservations in {{workspace}}?
reservations.onlyGone: Only for a worker that is gone. The server checks its heartbeat and process first and refuses if it is still alive.
reservations.body: This clears the dead worker's scan flag and releases only its own pending enqueues, so new scans and runs can start.
reservations.untouched: Busy, other workers' enqueues and a queued "process again" request are left as they are.

body.doc_file_path: Shows the real file name for this document. Secrets and emails stay masked. Recorded in the audit log.
body.doc_error: Shows the full error for this document. Secrets and emails stay masked. Recorded in the audit log.
body.job_name: Shows the real job name of the run in this workspace. Secrets and emails stay masked. Recorded in the audit log.

reveal.hideNote: Hidden again after {{seconds}} seconds unless you choose Keep visible.
reveal.kept: Kept visible until you hide it or leave
reveal.notFound: The value is gone: the document or the job changed since the page was drawn. Refresh and try again.

audit.title: Audit
audit.scope: Console actions, reveals, exports and log searches, plus admin changes: impersonation, workspace deletion, owners, server providers and cross-workspace document changes.
audit.emptyFiltered: No audit rows match these filters.
audit.note: Each action writes an intent row before it acts and a result row after. Without dates the last 30 days are shown (at most 400). Deleted workspaces show as a hash.

export.title: Export the audit log
export.body: Downloads the rows that match the current filters as CSV. Cells that would start a spreadsheet formula are escaped. The export and its reason are recorded in the audit log.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.off: Alerts are turned off on this server (OPS_ALERTS_ENABLED=false): no alert history is recorded and no alert email is sent.

emailMode.recordOnly: Record only: alert email is off (OPS_ALERT_EMAIL=false). Alerts are recorded here and nobody is emailed.
emailMode.noRecipients: Alert email is on, but no recipients are set (OPS_ALERT_EMAIL_TO or ALERT_EMAIL_TO), so nobody is emailed.
emailMode.on_one: Critical and serious alerts are emailed to {{count}} recipient: once when an alert opens and once when it resolves.
emailMode.on_other: Critical and serious alerts are emailed to {{count}} recipients: once when an alert opens and once when it resolves.
emailMode.onUnknown: Critical and serious alerts are emailed: once when an alert opens and once when it resolves.
emailMode.failures_one: {{count}} send failed since the last success.
emailMode.failures_other: {{count}} sends failed since the last success.

alerts.openSub: Worst first. An ack records who is on it; the alert stays open until its rule clears.
alerts.historySub: Newest first, kept 180 days. A rule that fires again after resolving opens a new alert.
alerts.noneHistory: No resolved alerts in the last 180 days.

thresholdError.order: Must be past the warning level.

rules.sub: The §1.7 defaults, with any server-wide changes. Changes apply from the next evaluation and are audited.
rules.saveBody: These thresholds apply on every worker from the next evaluation (within a minute). The change and its reason are recorded in the audit log.

ack.title: Ack “{{title}}”
ack.body: Records that you are on it. The alert stays open until its rule clears, and its resolve email is still sent.

mute.title: Mute “{{rule}}” for {{duration}}
mute.body: The rule is still evaluated and its alerts are still recorded and listed. No alert email is sent for it until the mute ends.

unmute.title: End the mute of “{{rule}}”
unmute.body: Alert email for this rule resumes from the next evaluation.

maintenance.explain: While maintenance mode is on, alerts are still evaluated and recorded, but no alert email is sent and the header reads Maintenance. It ends by itself.

start.title: Start maintenance mode
start.body: Use it for a deploy or a planned change. Alerts are still recorded; alert email is held until it ends.

end.title: End maintenance mode
end.body: Alert email resumes for alerts that are still open.

email.title: Alert email is NOT being delivered.

reason.send_failed: Recent alert emails failed to send
reason.no_recipients: No recipients are set (OPS_ALERT_EMAIL_TO or ALERT_EMAIL_TO)
reason.unknown: The alert channel reports a problem

maintenance.title: Maintenance mode until {{time}}
maintenance.effect: Alerts are still recorded; alert email is held.

alertDrawer.notFound: This alert no longer exists. Alert history is kept 180 days.

incident.title: Export incident timeline
incident.body: Downloads the alerts, audit rows, runs and system markers in a window as NDJSON. No log text is included, everything is redacted on the server and the rows are capped. The export and its reason are recorded in the audit log.

problem.order: The end must be after the start.
problem.too_long: The window can span at most 31 days.

incident.operatorOnly: Only operators can export the incident timeline.

events.title: System events
events.sub: Deployments, model changes, provider rejections, ingestion, orphaned runs and admin actions, merged from usage events, the audit log and runs.
events.none: No system events in the last {{window}}.

capture.title: Capture INFO lines
capture.body: Stores INFO lines from one module, on every worker, for at most 60 minutes. The capture stops by itself and its volume is capped. Lines are redacted like every other stored line. The capture and its reason are recorded in the audit log.
capture.moduleHint: A module or logger name, as in the Module filter. The server accepts only modules on its allowlist.
capture.stopBody: New INFO lines stop being stored on every worker. Lines already stored stay until retention removes them.
capture.none: INFO lines are not stored by default.
capture.operatorOnly: Only operators can capture INFO lines.
capture.sinkOff: This server does not store log lines (OPS_LOG_SINK is off).

tail.off: Live tail reads each process's own log file, and those files are off on this server. An operator turns them on with OPS_JSONL_LOGS=true.
tail.empty: No {{level}} lines from the live processes yet.
tail.truncated: Some process files were cut short or left out (the read budget); the oldest of their lines may be missing.
tail.capped: Showing the newest {{cap}} lines. Older ones are in each process's log file.
tail.footer: {{count}} lines · redacted when written and again when read
tail.note: Live tail filters by level and module only, and includes INFO. Lines come from the processes running now and from ones that exited in the last few minutes; use Stream for stored WARNING+ lines from any time in the last 7 days.

gpu.title: GPU {{index}}
gpu.noGpus: The exporter answered but listed no GPUs.
gpu.noHistory: No samples in this window yet.
gpu.sub: From the GPU exporter, every probe cycle (30 s)
gpu.exporterDown: The GPU exporter did not answer ({{error}}). The last numbers it gave are below.
gpu.historySub: Per GPU, from the probe rows
gpu.note: Read from the nvidia_gpu_exporter sidecar over the compose network; the API container has no GPU access of its own. vLLM's KV cache and queues stay on the embedding and rerank cards.
gpu.off: GPU metrics are off on this server. With the GPU preset, an operator enables the exporter sidecar in the setup wizard and sets OPS_GPU_EXPORTER_URL. Until then, vLLM's KV cache on the embedding and rerank cards is the only GPU signal.
gpu.noReading: No reading from the GPU exporter yet. The first one arrives with the next probe cycle.

admin.viewFailed: This view could not be shown. Choose another view or reload the page.

acting.label: Acting on another workspace
acting.title: Acting on workspace {{workspace}}.
acting.body: Documents shows and changes this workspace, not your own. Every change you make there is audited.
